title: Royal tomb theory and the lack of mummies in Khufu's and Khafre's pyramids
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Royal tomb theory and the lack of mummies in Khufu's and Khafre's pyramids, about c. 2500 BC at Egypt (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Most Egyptologists believe the Great Pyramid was built for the pharaoh Khufu around 2500 BC as part of a massive funerary complex designed [music] to help the king ascend to the afterlife. And the Pyramid of Khafre was, of course, built for the tomb of pharaoh Khafre, Khufu's son. But, no confirmed mummies or tombs [music] of Khufu or Khafre have ever been found inside of the pyramids.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, notes that most experts on ancient Egypt believe the Great Pyramid at Giza was built around 2500 BC as a tomb for the king Khufu, and the next pyramid as a tomb for his son Khafre. But Michels points out that no confirmed mummies or burial chambers of either king have ever been found inside. He raises this in an episode about a claimed energy grid under the pyramids, as a hint that they may have served some other purpose.
